dedupe_keys.name: teva spot toolkit sensor placement for contaminant warning systems

description: The TEVA-SPOT Toolkit (SPOT) supports the design of contaminant warning systems that use real-time sensors to detect contamination in municipal water distribution networks. It treats sensor placement as an optimisation problem and lets the user choose among performance objectives such as population health effects, time to detection, extent of contamination, volume consumed and number of failed detections; required or forbidden locations and per-location installation costs can be added as constraints. It was developed at Sandia National Laboratories by Berry, Riesen, Hart, Phillips and Watson (release 1.2, April 2008) and is published as open source in C++, C and Python under the BSD 3-clause licence, recorded in DOE CODE. Caveats: the release dates from 2008 and relies on contamination simulations produced with EPANET-based tools, so it needs a calibrated network model and incident scenarios as input. Simulation uses: optimising sensor networks for water security and emergency response in drinking water systems. Related records: EPANET (model-epanet) and WNTR (model-wntr).
inputs: Water distribution network model and contamination incident simulations (impact files)
Performance objectives, sensor budget, required or forbidden locations and installation costs
